You will not be able to handle this on your own, mostly because you're too close to the situation. She needs outside help.

Medication is trial and error. It will often take 3-4 attempts before finding a medication that works for someone. It can take many more. Each attempt is about a month of taking the medication every day to see if it has any effect. It takes about 2 weeks for the medication to kick in, and another two weeks to see how much effect it has.

Therapy and counselling is similar. People will often go to several therapists before finding one that they work well with. One popular modern technique is Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), in which the therapist teaches the patient "how to think" (for lack of a better definition), as opposed to talking about the patient's issues directly. Fortunately, you can usually tell after the first meeting if the therapist will be able to help you or not.

Unfortunately, treating depression is a lot of work. When you're "in the pit", you can't seek help yourself and you feel as if you don't deserve help. When you're no longer depressed, you feel as if "I'm not sick, I don't need help. Maybe when I'm feeling depressed again." People who are depressed will often need a push to go see someone.

I personally think medication is more effective than counselling, but research shows that the use of both together is the most effective.

It's a chemical imbalance in the brain.

Exercise is also a supporting factor in recovering and maintaining well being.

Our brain needs physical activity and the input that comes with it.

This doesn't mean that during a severe depression someone should be taken to a gym and be expected to work out for over an hour.

They might be able to do it once or twice, but likely the fatigue and stress will have it turn into a negative experience only further fueling despair and adversity for this kind of beneficial activity.

From my own experience just going for walks on a daily basis is a good way to start.

It takes time to get into a rhytm, so take that time.

Once she is excercising, try to track her actions and make notes of her accomplishments and hopefully progress.

After a few times you can create a chart to show what she has done and connect it to how she was feeling after working out.(Talk about what exercising does for her 1st)

Now she has a chart to help her stay focused and a reason to regularly do her exercises and see the progress and be reminded of how she felt better.

SpaceEngine (stylized as "Space Engine") is a free 3D astronomy program and game engine developed by Russian astronomer and programmer Vladimir Romanyuk. Using real astronomical catalogs and procedural generation, it creates a three-dimensional planetarium representing the entire universe. Users can travel through space in any direction or speed, and forwards or backwards in time. SpaceEngine is in beta status, and is currently freeware for Microsoft Windows. It uses pseudo-random numbers to procedurally create any kind of planetary system, nebula or galaxy.

One of the main features of the program is its scientific accuracy. Cataloged objects are based on real data, while procedural objects are built around the cataloged universe using realistic generation algorithms. Properties of objects, such as temperature, mass, radius, etc., are presented to the user on the HUD and in an accessible information window. Users can observe objects from small spacecraft to galaxy clusters, similar to other simulators such as Celestia. SpaceEngine includes thousands of real objects, including stars from the Hipparcos catalog, galaxies from the NGC and IC catalogs, several well-known nebulae, and all known extrasolar planets and their stars.

The next step is to pull in and quickly bump the upper arm into the chest/stomach and the knee goes toward the groin. This is to check A) for a "wire" and B) for a weapon concealed in a shoulder holster and a weapon concealed in the front of the pants.
